_comment: What tools/package-batch.js puts in this batch's upload package (batches/2026-10-b/upload/). Batch 2026-10-a's seven website patches are on the live branch (commit 39036014). This batch applies three new ones: mkpage-offer-box.patch (the first offer as the navy band), build-place-entries.patch (a numbered run of place headings is not counted as section questions) and contact-place-prefill.patch (the contact form's message starts with the place from a per-place offer's ?place= link). It also corrects Seasons' beach drive on the live 55+ pages: the corrected batch 2026-10-a spec and data files ship through copyAs, and the four 55+ pages are rebuilt with mkpage (rebuild); they are never patched. The data files go to the website's data/2026-10-b/, so data/photos.json (batch 2026-10-a's photo records) is not overwritten; the specs read data/2026-10-b/ and merge both photos.json files. Every photo the pages show is under /images/buyers/<page>/, so one images folder serves all five. The sitemap and llms.txt entries are made from the built pages; each page is listed after its own hub (listAfter). Round 15: mkpage-no-hero-cta.patch (heroCta: false means no offer under the short answer; the homes strips are the offer).

text.commit: Batch 2026-10-b: five buyer pages, inbound links, sitemap and llms files
text.specsRow: The five page specs and the batch's shared kit `_kit.js`.
text.dataRow: This batch's data files and its `photos.json`. The specs read them from here. The site's `data/photos.json` (batch 2026-10-a) is not changed; the specs read both.
text.stitch: the header and footer are unchanged; this keeps every page in step
pageChecks: The links in the page open, including the links to the other pages in this batch.

changes: `/buyers/first-time-home-buyer-myrtle-beach/` and `/buyers/relocating/which-town/` (with its spec, `data/relocating/pages/which-town.js`): a link to the affordable places page.

`/buyers/55-plus-communities/` and `/buyers/golf-communities/`: a link to the gated communities page; the golf page's FAQ answer on gates now says only what verified sources show. In the golf page's comparison table, the gate cells for Prestwick and Wachesaw Plantation now read "Gatehouse at the entrance" and Wachesaw East "Gate at the entrance" (they said a live guard around the clock, 24-hour security and security; no verified source shows staffing). Pawleys Plantation's cell no longer says "Gated" (no verified source shows it gated), and the HOA notes for Prestwick and Wachesaw East no longer list a guard or security.
`/submarkets/carolina-forest/`: a link to The Farm at Carolina Forest.
`sitemap.xml`: the five pages, with their photos (Google image sitemap). The four buyer pages are listed after the buyers hub, The Farm after Carolina Forest.
`llms.txt`: the five pages, with their descriptions.
`llms-full.txt`: regenerated by `node build.js llmsfull`, so it carries the five pages' text.

The four 55+ pages (`/buyers/55-plus-communities/` Del Webb North Myrtle Beach, Del Webb at Grande Dunes, Myrtle Trace, Seasons at Prince Creek West), rebuilt from their specs: Seasons' drive to the beach is about 13 minutes, not 10. The old figure ended at a Garden City walkover with no parking; 13 minutes is to GARDEN CITY 45, the nearest access with a lot (gated ledger row 176). On the Seasons page: the at-a-glance row, the FAQ answer, the map's beach dot and label; on all four, the Seasons row of the comparison table. Nothing else on those pages changes.
`tools/mkpage.js`: `mkpage-offer-box.patch`, the first offer as the same navy band as the last when a spec gives it a title. No live page changes.
`build.js`: `build-place-entries.patch`, a numbered run of 3 or more place headings is not counted as section questions (audit rule A22). No live page's result changes.

`tools/blog-brain-2026-10-b/` (new): the Blog-Brain page tools this batch was built and reviewed with (`page-kit.js`, `compare.js` and the files they load). `tools/blog-brain/`, which batch 2026-10-a's pages load, is not changed, so a rebuild of those pages gives the same HTML as today (its map data is older than this batch's).
